header:
Date: 2026-04-25 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Marta Reyes (Aquila Head of Platform), David Lin (Aquila SRE), Priya Mehta (Aquila Security Architect), Jon Park (Aquila Eng Manager)
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samira from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account. we also have Ethan our solutions engineer. can you all introduce quickly?
[00:11] Marta: sure, i'm marta, head of platform at aquila. we run a multi-region kubernetes fleet mostly gcp and aws, and exploring private deployment options for LLM inference.
[00:20] David: david here, sre, i'll be owning networking and the peering questions.
[00:25] Priya: priya, security architect, focused on encryption, audit logs, compliance.
[00:30] Jon: jon, eng manager, interested in perf and rollout plan.
[00:35] Ethan: great, thanks. quick agenda: understand your constraints—network, compliance, regions—then run through our private deployment options (VPC peering, private endpoints, dedicated), and capture next steps. sound good?
[00:46] Marta: yep that works.
[00:48] Samira: quick qualifier, what are you solving for? low latency for user-facing products, or data isolation for PII workloads?
[00:56] Jon: both, but first priority is isolation and residency, second is latency under 200ms tail for chat flows.
[01:05] Priya: and we need auditability and BYOK KMS integration—our compliance team insists.
[01:12] Ethan: ok good, that's a common pattern. on networking we offer a few options: 1) VPC peering to our managed VPC, 2) Private endpoints / PrivateLink style setup where our service sits behind an interface endpoint in your VPC, or 3) fully air-gapped on-prem or private deployment where control plane is local. each has tradeoffs around egress, NAT, and cross-region traffic.
[01:34] David: can you clarify peering vs endpoints—specifically about routed routes and flow logs, and whether traffic ever traverses public internet?
[01:43] Ethan: good question. with VPC peering the traffic is direct L3 routing between your VPC and ours—no egress to public internet. with private endpoints, we provision an interface endpoint in your VPC that talks over AWS private link (or equivalent) so again private path—both avoid public egress. the difference is peering is L3 and simpler for high-throughput but requires us to accept routes and you to accept routes; endpoints are more controlled and fit restrictive environments.
[02:10] Priya: do you support VPC peering across accounts and across regions? we have EU prod in eu-west1 and US staging in us-west2.
[02:19] Ethan: we can do cross-account peering. cross-region peering is supported but with some caveats—latency and egress costs can add up. for EU residency we recommend deploying Redwood Private control plane and inference nodes in the same region to keep data in-region.
[02:35] Marta: what's the model for KMS? we use aws-kms and also have an on-prem hsm for keys.
[02:41] Samira: we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS; we integrate with aws-kms and can integrate with customer HSM via key wrapping—there's an envelope encryption model. you'll have to share KMS policy for the service principal.
[02:55] Priya: and audit logs—do you ship syslogs to our SIEM or do we pull from your control plane?
[03:01] Ethan: both options—our private deployment supports forwarding audit logs to your syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver or we can allow read-only API access so you can pull logs. for strict compliance, many customers configure an external log sink in-region.
[03:12] David: any network ACL / security group limitations? we prefer deny-by-default and only allow specific CIDRs.
[03:18] Ethan: yes we support allow-lists. typically we provide the CIDR ranges you'll need to allow for peering or the private endpoint interface IPs. we also support IP allowlist for control plane access and admin consoles.
[03:29] Jon: performance—if we run dedicated capacity in our VPC, what latency can we expect vs hosted?
[03:36] Ethan: dedicated capacity colocated in your region will typically be on-par with hosted in same region; tail latency depends on model size and batching. for chat style low-latency we recommend smaller quantized models or the CPU/GPU mix we discussed in the docs. worst-case, tail might be 150-300ms depending on prompt length; with tuning (auto-batching and prefix cache) we can push under 200ms for most cases.
[03:58] Marta: cost conversation—is private deployment significantly more expensive?
[04:02] Samira: private has more fixed costs (reserved capacity, infra), but gives you predictable throughput and data isolation. Hosted is pay-as-you-go. we can produce a cost/latency comparison for your throughput profile.
[04:15] David: region constraints—we need all EU prod data to never leave eu-west1. how do you enforce that?
[04:21] Ethan: you can pin instances to region; our control plane can be run privately in your VPC or we can offer a customer-managed control plane so metadata and logs stay in-region. additionally, we configure egress controls and ensure no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled.
[04:36] Priya: what about dependencies like container registry or artifact pulls—do those require internet egress?
[04:41] Ethan: initial bootstrap may pull images; for private installs we can provide air-gapped bundles or you can mirror images to your registry. subsequent runtime does not require public egress.
[04:51] Jon: any support for multi-AZ within a region?
[04:54] Ethan: yes, for high availability we deploy nodes across AZs; routing within the VPC handles AZ failover.
[05:00] Marta: curious about private endpoints—does that mean we get ENIs in our subnets? what about route tables?
[05:06] Ethan: yes for PrivateLink-style endpoints we create interface endpoints (ENIs) in your subnets. route tables don't change like peering but you need to ensure subnet sizes and security groups allow the ENIs.
[05:19] David: and for logging and tracing, can we get per-request traces tied to our request-id?
[05:24] Ethan: yes we add tracing headers and emit request-level metadata to logs so you can correlate with your app traces. in private deployments you control the log sink.
[05:33] Priya: encryption at rest—we need to ensure model weights and caches are encrypted with our keys.
[05:38] Ethan: supported. we encrypt disk with customer-managed keys; for KV cache and ephemeral storage we also support encrypting with the same KMS envelope keys.
[05:47] Marta: ok, timeline—if we wanted a pilot in prod-eu with dedicated capacity, how long to stand up?
[05:53] Samira: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: initial security review, access to non-prod, then provision dedicated nodes and run a small workload. private deployment with BYOK and audit config tends to be towards 3-6 weeks depending on approvals.
[06:07] Jon: approvals—our legal will want SLAs and data processing agreement. do you have a template?
[06:12] Samira: yes we'll share our enterprise contract template and standard DPA with the security pack.
[06:16] Marta: one more, do you support VPC endpoints for both AWS and GCP?
[06:20] Ethan: yes we have equivalents: AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect. implementation differs slightly but we support both.
[06:28] David: are there any known gotchas for cross-cloud networking with multi-region services?
[06:33] Ethan: main things are egress billing and latency; also some cloud providers have limits on number of interface endpoints per VPC which can affect scaling. we usually recommend peering for heavy throughput and endpoints for restrictive security posture.
[06:48] Priya: about identity—can you integrate with our SAML SSO and RBAC?
[06:52] Samira: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, and RBAC roles. for private installs you can federate to your identity provider and sync groups.
[06:59] Jon: ok what's the next step from here?
[07:02] Samira: we'll send architecture doc, SOC2, standard network templates, and a cost/latency estimate. Ethan will do a quick baseline for models you mentioned. then we schedule an SE deep dive with your SREs.
[07:12] Marta: sounds good. also i'll share our VPC diagrams and CIDR ranges.
[07:16] David: i'll add the limits for interface endpoints and our firewall rules.
[07:20] Priya: i'll confirm the KMS vendor and compliance checklist.
[07:24] Ethan: perfect. any blockers right now?
[07:27] Jon: not really, just need to validate costs.
[07:30] Samira: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in an email with docs and calendar invites.
[07:35] Marta: thank you.
[07:36] (call ends)
